'''Valery Anatolyevich Rubakov''' ({{langx|ru|Валерий Анатольевич Рубаков}}, 16 February 1955 – 18 October 2022) was a Russian theoretical physicist. His scientific interests included [[quantum field theory]], [[elementary particle physics]], and [[cosmology]]. 

He was affiliated with the [[Institute for Nuclear Research]] (INR) of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in [[Moscow]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2022-12-29 |title=Valery Rubakov 1955–2022 |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/valery-rubakov-1955-2022/ |access-date=2023-01-25 |website=CERN Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Education==
Rubakov studied physics at [[Moscow State University]], graduating in 1978. He subsequently began doctoral work at the INR, completing his thesis in 1981.<ref name="INSPIRE-HEP">{{cite web | title=Rubakov, Valerii A. – Profile | website=INSPIRE-HEP | url=https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/V.A.Rubakov.1 | access-date=25 September 2018}}</ref>

==Scientific achievements==
Rubakov was among the best known of contemporary Russian physical theorists,<ref name="Pomeranchuk"/><ref name="CERN54"/> notable for his studies of the cosmological effects of gauge interactions and for the development of novel ideas of space-time and gravity.<ref name="Markov"/>

Rubakov first came to prominence for monopole catalysis of proton decay, a remarkable insight on contemporary field theory.<ref>{{cite journal| title=Superheavy Magnetic Monopoles and Proton Decay| last=Rubakov| first=V. A.| year=1981| journal=JETP Letters| volume=33| issue=12| pages=644–646}}</ref> [[Gerard 't Hooft|'t Hooft]] and [[Alexander Markovich Polyakov|Polyakov]] had shown that some [[Grand Unified Theories]] predict the existence of [['t Hooft–Polyakov monopole|massive magnetic monopoles]]. Rubakov pointed out such a monopole would induce proton decay, leaving an observable footprint in the form of electron neutrinos. The phenomenon was independently suggested by [[Curtis Callan]] and has become known as the [[Callan–Rubakov effect]].<ref name="Callan">{{cite journal | last=Callan | first=Curtis G. | title=Monopole catalysis of baryon decay | journal=Nuclear Physics B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=212 | issue=3 | year=1983 | issn=0550-3213 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(83)90677-6 | pages=391–400| bibcode=1983NuPhB.212..391C }}</ref>

Together with [[Mikhail Shaposhnikov]], Rubakov was one of the first to model spacetime and gravity using ideas from [[brane cosmology]].<ref name="Rubakov Shaposhnikov 1983">{{cite journal | last1=Rubakov | first1=V. A. | last2=Shaposhnikov | first2=M. E. | title=Do we live inside a domain wall? | journal=Physics Letters B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=125 | issue=2–3 | year=1983 | issn=0370-2693 | doi=10.1016/0370-2693(83)91253-4 | pages=136–138| bibcode=1983PhLB..125..136R }}</ref> Rubakov and Shaposhnikov conjectured that we live on a four-dimensional [[brane]] embedded in a higher-dimensional universe. Ordinary particles are confined in a potential well which is narrow along the additional dimensions, thereby localizing matter to the brane.<ref name="Markov"/>

Rubakov's paper with Shaposhnikov and [[Vadim Kuzmin (physicist)|Vadim Kuzmin]] on the effect of electroweak non-conservation of baryon and lepton numbers at high temperatures is considered fundamental to modern theory about the early universe.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=V. A. Kuzmin |author2=V. A. Rubakov |author3=M. E. Shaposhnikov | title = On anomalous electroweak baryon-number non-conservation in the early universe | journal = Physics Letters B | volume = 155 | date = 16 May 1985| issue = 1–2| pages = 36–42| doi= 10.1016/0370-2693(85)91028-7|bibcode = 1985PhLB..155...36K }}</ref>

Rubakov was the author of a well-regarded textbook on field theory.{{sfn|Rubakov|2002}}

He served as a member of the [[CERN]] Scientific Policy Committee from 2014 to 2019 and the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|ICTP]] Scientific Council from 2010 to 2020.<ref name=":0" />

== Awards ==
Rubakov was a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences since 1998. He was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.amacad.org/multimedia/pdfs/classlist2015.pdf| publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences| title=Newly elected members, April 2015| access-date=23 September 2018}}</ref>

In 1999 the Russian Academy of Sciences awarded Rubakov and Kuzmin the [[Friedmann Prize]] "for a series of works on the formation of the baryon asymmetry of the universe".<ref name="RAS">{{cite web | title=Премия имени А.А. Фридмана| trans-title=A. A. Friedmann Prize| website=Russian Academy of Sciences| url=http://www.ras.ru/win/db/award_dsc.asp?P=id-78.ln-ru| language=ru| access-date=25 September 2018| quote=За серию работ "Образование барионной ассиметрии Вселенной"}}</ref> He received the 2003 [[Institute for Theoretical and Experimental Physics|ITEP]] [[Isaak Yakovlevich Pomeranchuk|Pomeranchuk]] Prize "for pioneering contribution ''[sic]'' to developing and novel application of nonperturbative methods in field theory".<ref name="Pomeranchuk">{{cite web| title=Pomeranchuk prize winners 2003| website=[[Institute for Theoretical and Experimental Physics|ITEP]]| url=http://www.itep.ru/science/pomeranshuk/detail.php?ID=508 | access-date=24 September 2018}}</ref><ref name="CERN54">{{cite journal| url=https://cerncourier.com/faces-and-places-54/| journal=CERN Courier| volume=44| title=Dyson and Rubakov share the Pomeranchuk Prize for 2003| issue=1| page=44| year=2004| access-date=25 September 2018| archive-date=25 September 2018| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180925180511/https://cerncourier.com/faces-and-places-54/| url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2005 he was awarded the INR [[Moisey Alexandrovich Markov|Markov]] Prize for fundamental physics with {{ill|Mikhael Shaposhnikov|de|Шапошников, Михаил Евгеньевич|ru|Michail Jewgenjewitsch Schaposchnikow}}.<ref name="INR RAS">{{cite web| title=INR Markov Prize| website=Institute for Nuclear Research| url=https://www.inr.ac.ru/a/i/6441e.htm| access-date=25 September 2018}}</ref><ref name="Markov">{{cite journal| url=https://cerncourier.com/faces-and-places-70/| title=Rubakov and Shaposhnikov win INR prize for fundamental physics| journal=CERN Courier| volume=45| issue=7| page=43| year=2005| access-date=24 September 2018| archive-date=25 September 2018| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180925180613/https://cerncourier.com/faces-and-places-70/| url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2008 he won the [[J. Hans D. Jensen]] Prize of the [[University of Heidelberg]],<ref name="Jensen">{{cite web| website=Institute for Theoretical Physics of the University of Heidelberg| title=Jensen Professoren| language=de| == Personal life and death ==
In February 2022, Rubakov signed an open letter by Russian scientists condemning the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://t-invariant.org/2022/02/we-are-against-war/ |title=Открытое письмо российских учёных и научных журналистов против войны с Украиной |date=24 February 2022 |access-date=2 April 2022 |language=ru |trans-title=An open letter from Russian scientists and scientific journalist against the war in Ukraine}}</ref>

Rubakov died on 18 October 2022, at age 67, following complications from [[COVID-19]] that he had contracted in September.  He had been in [[Sarov]] at the time of his death, lecturing.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Roscoe |first1=Matthew |title=Russian Academy of Sciences theoretical physicist Valery Rubakov dies suddenly aged 68 following "Covid complications" |url=https://euroweeklynews.com/2022/10/19/russian-academy-of-sciences-physicist-valery-rubakov-dies-suddenly-covid-complications/ |access-date=19 October 2022 |work=Euro Weekly News |date=19 October 2022}}</ref>
